precepts.text: But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream. Let judgment run down. Do not waver and get around it; do not force the course to divert it.
precepts.point: A double minded man is unstable in all his ways: always tossed around, never steady, never going head on.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
The one who wavers is trying to dodge correction, to force the course of the river. Amos shows the river as it should flow: “But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.”

That is a river. Let judgment run down as waters. Let it run. Don’t waver and try to get around it; don’t try to force the course to divert it. Let judgment come down, and righteousness as a mighty stream.

You asked God to show you your errors, and he is showing you. “For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed. For let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord.” If you keep rerouting the judgment away from yourself, you will not receive the wisdom you asked for. Let it run down on you, accept it, and fix what it shows you.

precepts.text: They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly. So they will pass laws to make the reprover an offender for his words: hate speech, terrorism, treason, unpatriotic. Lock him up. They will do it because they can.
precepts.point: They make a man an offender for a word: say certain things and you face jail time, imprisonment, exile, fines, firing. And they lay a snare for him that reproveth in the gate: traps for the ones teaching in the streets.

note.label: The Religious Peer Pressure of Fred Price Jr

precepts.why:
Isaiah says the terrible one, Edom, is brought to nought: the one that does terrible things to the nations behind the cloak, behind the scenes, to maintain power and authority on the earth, destroyed as Ezekiel 35 said. The scorner is consumed, and all that watch for iniquity are cut off, those “That make a man an offender for a word, and lay a snare for him that reproveth in the gate.” Who is the one that reproveth in the gate? Amos answers: “They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly.”

They hate him that rebukes in the gate, in the streets. They abhor him that speaks uprightly. That is the one teaching in the streets, and that is who they lay the snares for, in the legal system, in their music and their media.

So they will pass laws to make those of us who reprove offenders for our words. Say certain things and you face jail time, imprisonment, exile, banishment; they are even trying to pass laws where you can be put to death, talking about bringing back beheadings and the guillotine. They will call it hate speech, terrorism, treason, being unpatriotic. You are anti-MAGA, against abortion, against same-sex, against white supremacy? Lock that brother up, lock that sister up. You say you are an Israelite, that they are fake Jews? Hate speech; five years; fire them from their job; fine them thousands; put a lien on their house.

They will do it because they can, and they will. But the most frightening one to them is the one they cannot kill, the righteous one they cannot pay off, bribe, drug, slander, poison or shoot. And Isaiah’s end is sure: the terrible one is brought to nought, and all that lay snares for him that reproveth in the gate are cut off.

precepts.text: They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly. That includes some of your own mothers and fathers, brothers and sisters.
precepts.point: And judgment is turned away backward, and justice standeth afar off: for truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter. And he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey: when you repent and come to this truth, everybody around you starts hating you. And the Lord saw it, and it displeased him that there was no judgment.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
“Yea, truth faileth; and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey.” If you depart from evil by repenting, you make yourself a prey to everybody around you; everybody around you hates your guts now. Amos says the same thing: “They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly.”

That includes some of your own mothers and fathers, sisters and brothers. They hate the one who rebukes and abhor the one who speaks uprightly, because “truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter.”

“and the Lord saw it, and it displeased him that there was no judgment.” There was no true judgment in the earth. The one who departs from evil is hated for it, and the Lord sees it.

precepts.text: For I know your manifold transgressions and your mighty sins: they afflict the just, they take a bribe, and they turn aside the poor in the gate from their right.
precepts.point: For it is not a light thing to do wickedly against the laws of God. Sometimes we take the laws of the Most High for granted with the mentality, I can sin and God won't do nothing.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
Jason promised the king “by intercession three hundred and threescore talents of silver, and of another revenue eighty talents.” What is that called? Bribery. He tried to bribe his way to become high priest. He paid money for an office that goes through bloodline.

Amos shows what the Lord thinks of it: “For I know your manifold transgressions and your mighty sins: they afflict the just, they take a bribe, and they turn aside the poor in the gate from their right.”

That is what they were doing back then. They take a bribe, they afflict the just, and the poor are turned aside from their right. Jason paid the bribe, the king took it, and Onias, the just high priest, was pushed out. The Lord knows those manifold transgressions and mighty sins.

precepts.text: Hate the evil, and love the good, and establish judgment in the gate: establish judgment in you, your household, your nation, and your communities, and it may be that the Lord God of hosts will be gracious unto the remnant of Joseph. David said, I love thy commandments, and I hate every false way. We are supposed to hate sin, hate that there is sin in our community, and do something about it by keeping God's law. We do not tolerate evil amongst our people.
precepts.point: They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly. Your treading is upon the poor; ye have built houses of hewn stone, but ye shall not dwell in them. Do not be comfortable, family; that is what Amos is saying.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.why:
Amos shows an Israel that hates the righteous: “They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly.” They tread upon the poor, build houses of hewn stone and plant pleasant vineyards, “but ye shall not dwell in them”. Don't be comfortable, family; that is what Amos is saying. A few verses on he tells them what to hate instead: “Hate the evil, and love the good”.

David said, I love thy commandments, and I hate every false way. We hate anything outside of keeping God's commandments: sin. We are supposed to hate sin, hate the fact that there is sin in our community, and do something about it by keeping God's law. We are not supposed to tolerate evil amongst our people.

Love the good is love God's commandments. That is your purpose, it is what increases your faith, and it is why you are called to magnify God's law.

“And establish judgment in the gate”: establish judgment in yourself, your household, your nation and your communities. Then “it may be that the Lord God of hosts will be gracious unto the remnant of Joseph.” You receive mercy when you hate the evil and love the good. That is the turn Amos calls for: stop hating the one who rebukes in the gate, and hate the sin instead. We separate ourselves from evil, the ways of our oppressor, and we strive for perfection.

precepts.text: Ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images, the star of your god, which ye made to yourselves. It is idolatry. God never gave us that star; Solomon picked it up dabbling in witchcraft.
precepts.point: Ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, and the star of your god Remphan, figures which ye made to worship them. Moloch is Baal, both the devil, and the star is the hexagram, which cannot be found anywhere in the Bible as God's sign.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
The Iranians burned large statues of a horned, bull-headed figure bearing the so-called Star of David, and they knew what they were doing: they were burning statues of Baal. That is not the Star of David. You cannot find it anywhere in the Bible; it is a sign in the occult.

Stephen said, “Yea, ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, and the star of your god Remphan, figures which ye made to worship them: and I will carry you away beyond Babylon.” If you didn't know, Moloch is Baal: the same thing, both the devil. The star is the star of their god, the devil, Baal or Moloch.

Stephen was quoting Amos: “But ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images, the star of your god, which ye made to yourselves.” Which ye made to yourselves: it is idolatry. God did not give us that star. When King Solomon was dabbling in witchcraft, that is how he got that star; God never gave it to us.

So the star so-called Israel and America carry is the star of Baal, and Baal worship shows up in plain sight: the bull's head statue at the 1933 Chicago World's Fair on Jewish Day, the giant mechanical bull at the 2022 Commonwealth Games, the bull on Wall Street. Even bullheaded, stupidly stubborn, comes from Baal worship, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. That idolatry is why Israel was carried away, and why we are in captivity today.

precepts.text: Go to Shiloh and see what I did to it; I will cast out Judah as I cast out the whole seed of Ephraim.
precepts.point: Amaziah, priest of Bethel, told Amos to go prophesy in Judah and not in the king's chapel. Amos was sent to his own people, as God always sends prophets to Israel alone.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
Amos warns Ephraim, “seek not Beth–el, nor enter into Gilgal”, for “Beth–el shall come to nought.” These were places built for worship by Abraham and Jacob, and Ephraim turned them into seats of idolatry. So Gilgal would surely go into captivity, and Beth–el would be destroyed. “Seek the Lord, and ye shall live; lest he break out like fire in the house of Joseph”: the house of Joseph is Ephraim.

Jeremiah turns the same judgment on Judah: “But go ye now unto my place which was in Shiloh, where I set my name at the first, and see what I did to it for the wickedness of my people Israel.” Go look at Shiloh and see what I did to it. “I spake unto you, rising up early and speaking, but ye heard not; and I called you, but ye answered not”: they refused the prophets.

“Therefore will I do unto this house, which is called by my name, wherein ye trust, and unto the place which I gave to you and to your fathers, as I have done to Shiloh. And I will cast you out of my sight, as I have cast out all your brethren, even the whole seed of Ephraim.” What was done to Ephraim will be done to Judah: the heathen come in, destroy the sanctuary and lead them captive. The exact same way. The same thing happens to both houses, both kingdoms. He raised up Assyria to overthrow Ephraim, and he raised up Babylon to overthrow Judah.

And they would not hear it. Amaziah the priest of Bethel, one of the low-level priests raised up that was not Levi, told Amos, “go, flee thee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there: But prophesy not again any more at Beth–el: for it is the king’s chapel”. Go teach Judah; you are disturbing the king's church. Amos was blitzing the churches. But the Lord said to him, “Go, prophesy unto my people Israel.” The Lord always sent his prophets to his people, and his people alone, to repent. It is the same with Jacob today: the one preaching the word of God is called a troublemaker.

So Bethel came to nought as Shiloh did, and Israel went “into captivity forth of his land”: their wives made harlots, their sons and daughters fallen by the sword, their land divided by line as it is to this day, dying “in a polluted land”. That began with the northern kingdom, but eventually it happened to all of us as a whole.

precepts.text: Let judgment run down as waters and righteousness as a mighty stream: that is how it keeps rising.
precepts.point: The water is risen so high now it cannot be passed over. You cannot get around us, and every one of you can answer for your faith.

note.label: Radicalize The Youth

precepts.text: The judges of Israel came to afflict the just and take a bribe, turning aside the poor in the gate from their right.
precepts.point: Israel's judges later fell into exactly this: they became covetous and took bribes to clear the guilty and turn aside the poor in the gate.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
Israel’s judges later fell into exactly what Numbers 35 forbade. “For I know your manifold transgressions and your mighty sins: they afflict the just, they take a bribe, and they turn aside the poor in the gate from their right.”

They became covetous and took bribes to clear the guilty and turn aside the poor in the gate. The satisfaction the law said never to take for a murderer became the bribe that afflicted the just, and the Lord counted it among Israel’s mighty sins.

precepts.text: Israel bore the tabernacle of Molech and the star of their god, the six-pointed star that came from the idolatry of Solomon's day.
precepts.point: Solomon built high places for Chemosh the abomination of Moab and for Molech the abomination of Ammon, and did likewise for all his strange wives who burnt incense and sacrificed to their gods. The six-pointed star called the star of David is in truth the star of Molech, an idol, and has nothing to do with righteousness.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

precepts.why:
“But ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images, the star of your god, which ye made to yourselves.” Israel bore the tabernacle of Molech and the star of their god, and that six-pointed star came from the idolatry of Solomon's day.

When Solomon was old, “his wives turned away his heart after other gods”, and he built “an high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab”, “and for Molech, the abomination of the children of Ammon.” The six-pointed star called the star of David is in truth the star of Molech, an idol. It has nothing to do with righteousness.

David also sinned, but when David sinned he repented and turned back, while Solomon kept going into sin. That is why Solomon's heart “was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father”, for a righteous man falls seven times and rises again.

precepts.text: Take away the noise of thy songs, for the Most High will not hear the melody of thy viols; gospel music without understanding is rejected.
precepts.point: Flood your mind with spiritual songs that prophesy within the music, like the albums coming out on Original Royalty, because the Most High wants to hear righteous songs, not the noise of the world.

note.label: Psalm 47: God the Great King Over All the Earth

precepts.why:
“sing ye praises with understanding.” Not the gospel hymns of the Christian church sung with no understanding; the Most High hates music without understanding. He says so: “Take thou away from me the noise of thy songs; for I will not hear the melody of thy viols.” Gospel music without understanding is rejected; to him it is noise.

So flood your mind with spiritual songs that prophesy within the music, like the albums coming out on Original Royalty. The Most High wants to hear righteous songs, praises with understanding, not the noise of the world.

precepts.text: As Israel repents and returns, righteous songs of praise are rising again in place of the songs of captivity.
precepts.point: He prays the wicked be consumed from the earth, and again charges his soul to bless the Lord.

note.label: Psalm 104: The Most High Clothed with Majesty over Creation

precepts.why:
“Take thou away from me the noise of thy songs; for I will not hear the melody of thy viols.” The songs of a rebellious Israel were noise to the Most High; he would not hear them.

Set that against David: “My meditation of him shall be sweet: I will be glad in the Lord.” The song he accepts comes from the one whose meditation is of him, who prays that the sinners be consumed out of the earth and the wicked be no more, and who charges his own soul, “Bless thou the Lord, O my soul.”

As Israel repents and returns, righteous songs of praise are rising again in place of the songs of captivity, songs the Most High will hear.

precepts.text: Paul is jealous over Israel with godly jealousy, having espoused them to one husband, to present them as a chaste virgin to Christ.
precepts.point: The virgin of Israel is falling into all types of sin and sacrificing to other gods; we are supposed to be a chaste virgin, but the virgin of Israel played the harlot.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

precepts.why:
“The virgin of Israel is fallen; she shall no more rise: she is forsaken upon her land”. We are supposed to be a chaste virgin. Paul is jealous over Israel with godly jealousy: “I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.”

But the virgin of Israel played the harlot, falling into all types of sin and sacrificing to other gods. That is the lamentation taken up against the house of Israel: the chaste virgin espoused to one husband is fallen, and there is none to raise her up.

precepts.text: Thou shalt build a house and not dwell therein, and plant a vineyard and not gather the grapes; the same curse first pronounced in Deuteronomy.
precepts.point: Forasmuch as their treading is upon the poor and they take from him burdens of wheat, they have built houses of hewn stone but shall not dwell in them, and planted pleasant vineyards but shall not drink the wine of them. These curses are generational from each captivity, the same thing repeating over and over.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

precepts.why:
“ye have built houses of hewn stone, but ye shall not dwell in them; ye have planted pleasant vineyards, but ye shall not drink wine of them.” This is the same curse first pronounced in Deuteronomy: “thou shalt build an house, and thou shalt not dwell therein: thou shalt plant a vineyard, and shalt not gather the grapes thereof.”

These curses are generational from each captivity, the same thing repeating over and over. Because their treading is upon the poor and they take from him burdens of wheat, and because they hate him that rebukes in the gate and abhor him that speaks uprightly, which they do the same today, the curse of Deuteronomy falls on them again.

precepts.text: The law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good; the just are those seeking righteousness and keeping the commandments.
precepts.point: Therefore the prudent shall keep silence in that time, for it is an evil time.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

precepts.why:
“they afflict the just, they take a bribe, and they turn aside the poor in the gate from their right.” Who are the just? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” The just are those seeking righteousness and keeping the commandments.

So the manifold transgressions and mighty sins the Most High knows are against the ones keeping his law, and against the poor, whom they turn aside in the gate as though they do not even see them, which is not the spirit of Christ. Therefore the prudent keep silence in that time, for it is an evil time.

precepts.text: Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites, the tribal god also known as Molech or Malcham.
precepts.point: But ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images, the star of your god which ye made to yourselves. This was going on even during the time of Solomon.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

precepts.why:
“But ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images, the star of your god, which ye made to yourselves.” This was going on even during the time of Solomon: “Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.” Milcom, the tribal god of the Ammonites, is also known as Molech or Malcham, the Moloch whose tabernacle Israel bore.

Instead of judgment running down as waters and righteousness as a mighty stream, the house of Israel carried the god of the Ammonites, even in Solomon's day.

points: Thus saith the Lord God: the city that went out by a thousand shall leave a hundred, and that which went forth by a hundred shall leave ten to the house of Israel.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

points: Thus saith the Lord unto the house of Israel, seek ye me and ye shall live, but seek not Bethel, nor enter into Gilgal, and pass not to Beersheba, for Gilgal shall surely go into captivity and Bethel shall come to nought.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

points: Seek the Lord and ye shall live, lest he break out like fire in the house of Joseph and devour it, and there be none to quench it in Bethel. If you worship these other gods and visit these other cities, the Lord will throw down everything.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

points: Ye who turn judgment to wormwood and leave off righteousness in the earth, seek him that makes the seven stars and Orion, turns the shadow of death into the morning, makes the day dark with night, and calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out upon the face of the earth; the Lord is his name.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

points: He strengthens the spoiled against the strong, so that the spoiled shall come against the fortress.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

points: They hate him that rebukes in the gate and abhor him that speaks uprightly, and they do the same thing today.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

points: Forasmuch as their treading is upon the poor and they take from him burdens of wheat, they have built houses of hewn stone but shall not dwell in them, and planted pleasant vineyards but shall not drink the wine of them. These curses are generational from each captivity, the same thing repeating over and over.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

points: For the Most High knows their manifold transgressions and mighty sins: they afflict the just, take a bribe, and turn aside the poor in the gate from their right, acting like they do not even see the poor, which is not the spirit of Christ.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

points: Therefore the prudent shall keep silence in that time, for it is an evil time.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

points: Seek good and not evil, that ye may live, and so the Lord the God of hosts shall be with you as ye have spoken.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

points: Hate the evil and love the good, and establish judgment in the gate; it may be that the Lord God of hosts will be gracious unto the remnant of Joseph.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

points: Therefore the Lord the God of hosts says wailing shall be in all streets, they shall say in all the highways, alas, alas, and they shall call the husbandman to mourning and such as are skillful of lamentation to wailing.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

points: In all vineyards shall be wailing, for the Most High will pass through thee bringing judgment.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

points: Woe unto you that desire the day of the Lord; to what end is it for you? The day of the Lord is darkness and not light. This is a spirit checker; when you find yourself saying "I can't wait till Christ gets back," you had better examine yourself and get all the impurities out of you before that day, because you do not know what end it will be for you.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

points: It is as if a man fled from a lion and a bear met him, or went into the house, leaned his hand on the wall, and a serpent bit him. Shall not the day of the Lord be darkness and not light, even very dark with no brightness in it?

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

points: I hate, I despise your feast days, and I will not smell in your solemn assemblies. This is not talking about the feasts of the Lord, but about how Israel wanted to conduct the feast asking "is the Sabbath over yet," with no spirit whatsoever in it.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

points: Though ye offer burnt offerings and meat offerings, he will not accept them, nor regard the peace offerings of your fat beasts. Take away the noise of thy songs, for he will not hear the melody of thy viols; he does not want to hear anything, because we are not living according to the commandments.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

points: But let judgment run down as waters and righteousness as a mighty stream. Have ye offered unto me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness forty years, O house of Israel?

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

points: But ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images, the star of your god which ye made to yourselves. This was going on even during the time of Solomon.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

points: Therefore the Most High will cause them to go into captivity beyond Damascus, saith the Lord, whose name is the God of hosts.
